actions.create_row.description: Creates a single new row in a BigQuery table. Column fields are loaded from the table schema.
actions.create_row.props.values.descript: Enter a value for each column. Fields are loaded from the table schema.
actions.create_rows.description: Creates new rows of data in a BigQuery table (accepts an array of row objects). Rows are available to query within seconds.
actions.create_rows.props.ignore_unknown: If enabled, fields not in the table schema are silently discarded. If disabled (default), unknown fields cause the row to fail.
actions.create_rows.props.rows.descripti: An array of row objects to insert. Keys must match the table column names. Example: `[{"name": "Alice", "age": 30}, {"name": "Bob", "age": 25}]`
actions.create_rows.props.skip_invalid_r: If enabled, valid rows are inserted even when some rows in the batch are invalid. If disabled (default), the entire batch fails if any row is invalid.
actions.custom_api_call.description: Make a custom API call to a specific endpoint
actions.custom_api_call.props.failsafe.d: On a failed request, output the error instead of failing the step.
actions.custom_api_call.props.followRedi: Follow 3xx redirects instead of returning them as the response.
actions.custom_api_call.props.headers.de: Authorization headers are injected automatically from your connection.
actions.custom_api_call.props.response_i: Enable for files like PDFs, images, etc.
actions.custom_api_call.props.timeout.de: Seconds to wait for a response. Empty: up to the flow limit (10 min).
actions.delete_rows.description: Deletes one or more rows from a BigQuery table using a SQL WHERE condition.
actions.delete_rows.props.location.descr: Dataset location (e.g. US, EU). Leave blank to use the default.
actions.delete_rows.props.where_clause.d: SQL condition to match the rows to delete. Do not include the WHERE keyword. Example: `status = "inactive" AND created_at < "2023-01-01"`
actions.find_one_row.description: Find a single row by specifying a WHERE clause and an optional ORDER BY. Returns the first matching row, or empty if none found.
actions.find_one_row.props.location.desc: Dataset location (e.g. US, EU). Leave blank to use the default.
actions.find_one_row.props.order_by.desc: Optional column(s) to sort results before picking the first row. Example: `created_at DESC`
SQL condition to filter rows. Do not include the WHERE keyword. Example: `email = "user@example.com"`
actions.find_or_create_row.description: Searches for a row matching a WHERE clause. If found, returns it. If not found, inserts the provided row data and returns that.
actions.find_or_create_row.props.create_: A JSON object of column/value pairs to insert if no matching row exists. Example: `{"email": "user@example.com", "name": "Alice"}`
actions.find_or_create_row.props.locatio: Dataset location (e.g. US, EU). Leave blank to use the default.
actions.find_or_create_row.props.where_c: SQL condition to search for an existing row. Do not include WHERE. Example: `email = "user@example.com"`
actions.get_rows_for_job.description: Retrieves the result rows from a completed BigQuery query job by Job ID. Use this after a "Query Job Completed" trigger to fetch the full result set.
actions.get_rows_for_job.props.job_id.de: The BigQuery job ID to fetch results for. This is returned by the "Query Job Completed" trigger or a "Run a Query" action.
Dataset location where the job ran (e.g. US, EU). Leave blank for US.
actions.get_rows_for_job.props.max_resul: Maximum number of rows to return (up to 10,000). Default: 1,000.
actions.import_data.description: Imports a batch of rows into a BigQuery table. Accepts a JSON array or newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON). Large datasets are automatically split into chunks.
actions.import_data.props.data.descripti: The data to import. Provide a JSON array of objects (`[{...}, {...}]`) or a newline-delimited JSON string where each line is one row object.
actions.import_data.props.ignore_unknown: Silently drop fields not present in the table schema. Default: off (fail on unknown fields).
actions.import_data.props.skip_invalid_r: Continue importing valid rows even if some rows fail validation. Default: off (fail entire batch).
actions.run_query.description: Execute a SQL query on BigQuery and return the results as flat rows
actions.run_query.props.location.descrip: Geographic location of your dataset (e.g. US, EU, us-central1). Leave blank for US.
actions.run_query.props.max_results.desc: Maximum number of rows to return (up to 10,000)
actions.run_query.props.query.descriptio: The SQL query to run. Uses standard SQL syntax. Example: `SELECT * FROM \`my_dataset.my_table\` LIMIT 100`
actions.run_query.props.use_legacy_sql.d: Enable only if your query uses BigQuery Legacy SQL syntax (not recommended)
actions.update_rows.description: Updates one or more existing rows in a BigQuery table using SQL SET and WHERE expressions.
actions.update_rows.props.location.descr: Dataset location (e.g. US, EU). Leave blank to use the default.
actions.update_rows.props.set_expression: Comma-separated column assignments. Do not include the SET keyword. Example: `status = "active", updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()`
actions.update_rows.props.where_clause.d: SQL condition to match the rows to update. Do not include the WHERE keyword. Example: `id = "abc123"`
description: Query, analyze, and stream data into Google BigQuery — the fully managed, serverless data warehouse
triggers.new_job_completed.description: Triggers when any BigQuery job (query, load, copy, or extract) finishes. Returns the job metadata including status, type, and timing.
triggers.new_job_completed.props.include: If enabled, jobs that completed with an error are also returned. Default: off (only successful jobs).
triggers.new_row.description: Triggers when a new row is added to a BigQuery table. Polls every 5 minutes by comparing the latest value in a sort column against the previous check.
triggers.new_row.props.max_results.descr: Maximum number of new rows to return per poll (default: 500).
triggers.new_row.props.sort_column.descr: Name of the column used to detect new rows. The table is ordered by this column (DESC) and any row newer than the last check is returned. Use a TIMESTAMP or DATETIME column, e.g. `created_at`.
triggers.query_job_completed.description: Triggers when a BigQuery query job finishes successfully. Each flow run receives the job metadata and the result rows from that query.
triggers.query_job_completed.props.max_r: Maximum number of result rows to fetch per completed job (default: 500).
triggers.updated_row.description: Triggers when an existing row is updated in a BigQuery table. Requires an `updated_at` TIMESTAMP column that is set whenever a row changes.
triggers.updated_row.props.created_at_co: If provided, only rows where the updated timestamp is newer than the created timestamp are returned, excluding brand-new rows from the results.
triggers.updated_row.props.max_results.d: Maximum number of updated rows to return per poll (default: 500).
triggers.updated_row.props.updated_at_co: Name of the TIMESTAMP column that records when a row was last updated, e.g. `updated_at`. Rows where this column is newer than the last check are returned.
